moduleTitle: Lesson 6 - Mobile Scan: Native, Hybrid & Web Apps
learningObjectives: Run the Mobile Scan wizard end to end: prepare the environment, connect a device, and scan.
Scan a native app and understand what gets captured as a Module.
Switch between native context and webview context when scanning a hybrid app.
Scan a mobile website through the device's own browser.
Configure Desired Capabilities and reusable Capability Sets in the Mobile Scan wizard.

elements.description: Mobile Scan creates Modules for native, hybrid and mobile web applications. Prepare the environment, select a connection, device and application, then select controls. Adding device/application entries is optional when suitable entries already exist.

elements.title: Running a scan
items: Right-click a Module folder and choose Scan > Mobile.
Select the connection, device and application; add missing entries if needed.
Set the optional preview, reset and capability choices, then Connect and choose Mobile Scan.
Select controls in Live View or Advanced View, review identification and save the Module.

elements.text: A scan connection does not validate all execution settings. Compare effective configuration and use the documented endpoint format without assuming a universal trailing-slash parsing defect.

bulletPoints: Prepare environment → start Mobile Scan → connect device → capture controls — one flow, all three app types.
A working scan connection is not proof the TMAServer TCP is correctly formatted for TestCase execution.

elements.description: Select connection, Select device and Select application organize the target choices. Local/Remote TMA connections can show installed apps, not merely apps scanned before.

Set capabilities opens named capability sets. Configure supported names and values for the actual driver; Appium extension capabilities use the appium: namespace, while standard WebDriver capabilities are distinct.

Add capabilities set creates a named group; Add capability adds an entry to the selected group. Select Capability Set applies that group to the scan. It is not a separate one-off versus reusable mechanism.

elements.text: For a UiAutomator2 Android session, autoGrantPermissions applies to supported runtime permissions and has target SDK/API requirements; special permissions need separate handling. For XCUITest on iOS, autoAcceptAlerts includes privacy alerts. They are driver-specific examples, not a universal two-setting bundle or proof that permission behavior has been tested.

elements.title: Wizard controls alongside Connect
items: Run Live View — enables the application preview for control selection.
Reset application — requests reset of application user settings/permissions and restart; verify the resulting state.
Set capabilities — selects the capability set used for the scan connection.

bulletPoints: Add capability adds an entry inside a named capability set.
Use the documented capabilities for the selected driver/platform.
Scan capabilities and execution capabilities need their respective configuration.

elements.description: Select controls in Live View or via Advanced View checkboxes and inspect the properties actually exposed by the application/engine. Choose an identification strategy that uniquely identifies the target; do not assume every app exposes the same useful metadata.

elements.text: Control identification quality depends heavily on how well the app under test exposes accessibility metadata. A poorly-labelled app (generic resource-ids, no accessibility labels) produces weaker, less stable identification — the mobile equivalent of a web page with no useful CSS selectors or test-ids.

bulletPoints: Inspect exposed properties and identification uniqueness rather than relying on a universal property list.
Weak metadata can reduce identification reliability and should be investigated with the application team.

elements.description: A hybrid app wraps one or more web views inside a native shell. From the outside it looks and behaves like a native app, but part or all of its content is actually rendered as HTML/CSS/JS inside an embedded browser engine.
When Mobile Scan detects a hybrid app, select Native for its native controls or Web and the appropriate webview for embedded content. Re-select the context when scanning another screen if prompted.

elements.text: Missing web controls can involve the selected context, WebView debugging, browser compatibility or application configuration. Check the actual context and prerequisites; do not infer a single cause from the symptom.

bulletPoints: Choose Native or Web and the intended webview for hybrid scanning.
Context selection is one diagnostic check, not a guaranteed root cause.

elements.term: The device's own browser, scanned in its device context
elements.description: Mobile Scan opens a website on the selected device, emulator or simulator. This exercises that target’s browser environment; a resized desktop viewport alone does not validate the same browser/device behavior.

elements.text: An emulator or simulator scan is not a physical-device test. Scanning identifies controls; runtime gestures and user behavior still require execution and validation.

bulletPoints: Scan the chosen mobile target and validate execution separately.

examPitfalls.title: Reaching for XBrowser to test a web app inside a mobile browser
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Testing a mobile website with a desktop XBrowser scan resized to a phone viewport.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Mobile Scan for the intended mobile target. Scanning and a resized desktop view do not by themselves certify physical-device gestures or behavior.

examPitfalls.title: Not switching context when scanning a hybrid app
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Trying to scan controls inside a hybrid app's embedded webview while the scan is still in native context, and seeing nothing get captured.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Choose Web and the correct webview when scanning embedded content; also check hybrid debugging and browser prerequisites.

examPitfalls.title: Trusting a successful scan connection as proof the TCP is correct
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Seeing the Mobile Scan's Add connection dialog connect fine, and assuming the same TMAServer value will work for execution too.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Compare effective scan/execution settings and documented endpoint formats. Do not invent a parser difference from a successful scan alone.

examPitfalls.title: Skipping the permissions/alerts capabilities and getting stuck on a popup
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Connecting without setting appium:autoGrantPermissions or appium:autoAcceptAlerts, then watching a scan or TestCase run stall on an Android runtime permission prompt or a native alert dialog it never expected.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use platform/driver-specific capability sets only when their behavior matches the test goal. Automatic permission/alert handling can hide flows that a permission test is meant to verify.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the correct high-level sequence for running a Mobile Scan?

options.text: Write the TestCase first, then scan to fill in the Modules it references.
Prepare the environment, select the connection/device/application, connect, select controls and save Modules.
Install the app under test through adb, then skip straight to execution.
Configure biometrics before any other setup.

practiceQuiz.hint: Environment and connection come before any control capture.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Prepare and choose the target before control selection. Add device/application entries only if needed; save the selected controls into Modules.

optionExplanations.A: This does not describe the scanner setup sequence.
optionExplanations.B: This follows target preparation and control selection.
optionExplanations.C: Installing alone does not create scanned Modules.
optionExplanations.D: Biometrics are not a universal first scan requirement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A hybrid app is being scanned in Native mode and the team needs its DOM-based embedded controls. Which selection should it check?

options.text: The app is actually a native app, not hybrid.
The scan is still in native context and needs to be switched to webview context.
The device needs to be rebooted.
TMA does not support hybrid apps at all.

practiceQuiz.hint: Native chrome and embedded webview content need different identification strategies.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Choose Web and the intended webview for embedded controls. This addresses the stated context mismatch; it does not rule out other WebView prerequisites.

optionExplanations.A: The scenario explicitly identifies a hybrid application.
optionExplanations.B: Web selection addresses the stated embedded-control context.
optionExplanations.C: A reboot does not address the stated context mismatch.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why is scanning a mobile website through the Mobile Scan preferred over a desktop XBrowser scan resized to a phone width?

options.text: XBrowser cannot render CSS at all.
It scans the selected mobile target’s browser environment rather than only changing a desktop viewport.
Resizing a desktop browser is not technically possible in Tosca.
Mobile web can only be scanned on iOS, never Android.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what's genuinely different between a real mobile browser and a resized desktop one.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The selected target provides its browser environment. If the target is virtual, this is still not physical-device evidence; execution remains necessary.

optionExplanations.B: The target browser environment differs from a desktop width change.
optionExplanations.C: Resizing impossibility is not the reason.
optionExplanations.D: Mobile web scanning is not iOS-only.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A scan exposes only generic identifiers and no useful labels for a native control. Which issue should the team investigate?

options.text: Mobile Engine 3.0 does not support native apps well.
The app itself exposes weak accessibility metadata, the mobile equivalent of a web page with no useful CSS selectors or test-ids.
The device needs a factory reset.
TMA is running an outdated version.

practiceQuiz.hint: Compare this to identifying a badly-instrumented web page.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Weak or non-unique exposed metadata can make identification unreliable. Inspect available properties and uniqueness instead of inferring a host or version failure without evidence.

optionExplanations.A: This does not establish that native support is absent.
optionExplanations.B: The given metadata is weak and warrants identification review.
optionExplanations.C: Erasing the device is not supported by this evidence.
optionExplanations.D: The scenario gives no version evidence.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Tosca Commander menu entry starts Mobile Scan?

options.text: Mobile option in Module Scanners
Tricentis Mobile License
CLI connection settings
Scratchbook feature

practiceQuiz.hint: Look at where you'd actually trigger a scan from inside Tosca Commander.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Scan > Mobile starts the documented scanner. Its presence alone does not prove licensing, device readiness or successful test execution.

optionExplanations.A: This is the documented scanner menu entry.
optionExplanations.B: A licence is not the menu command.
optionExplanations.C: CLI setup is not the scanner entry point.
optionExplanations.D: ScratchBook is an execution tool, not this scanner menu.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which two capability descriptions match their respective drivers, subject to documented prerequisites? (two correct answers)

options.text: UiAutomator2 autoGrantPermissions handles supported Android runtime permissions
XCUITest autoAcceptAlerts automatically accepts iOS alerts, including privacy prompts
The app under test is automatically reinstalled before every scan
TMAServer is automatically corrected to include a trailing slash

practiceQuiz.hint: These are separate platform-specific examples, not one universal bundle.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The driver documentation scopes autoGrantPermissions to supported Android permissions and autoAcceptAlerts to iOS alerts. Neither setting repairs an Agent URL or requires reinstalling the target app in every session.

optionExplanations.A: This is the Android-driver permission behavior, within its prerequisites.
optionExplanations.B: This is the iOS-driver alert behavior, including privacy prompts.
optionExplanations.C: Neither named capability requires universal reinstallation.
optionExplanations.D: Neither capability rewrites the Agent address.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the Mobile Scan wizard's Capabilities dialog, what is the difference between Add capability and Add capability set?

options.text: There is no difference — both do the same thing.
Add capabilities set creates a named group; Add capability adds an entry to the selected group.
Add capability set only works with Remote (TMA) connections.
Add capability is for Android; Add capability set is for iOS.

practiceQuiz.hint: A named group contains individual capability entries.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Capabilities are added inside the selected set, which is then applied with Select Capability Set. Add capability is not documented as an ungrouped one-off session mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: A set and an entry have different roles.
optionExplanations.B: The documented workflow adds entries to named groups.
optionExplanations.C: Capability groups are not stated as remote-only.
optionExplanations.D: These controls are not split by Android versus iOS.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In an XCUITest iOS session, what does appium:autoAcceptAlerts do?

options.text: Grants every Android special permission
Allows manual interaction with alerts
Automates handling of pop-ups and alerts
Connects devices to the Tosca interface

practiceQuiz.hint: The iOS-driver capability includes privacy alerts as well as other supported alerts.
practiceQuiz.rationale: XCUITest can automatically accept iOS alerts, including privacy access prompts. It does not establish a device connection or grant every Android special permission.

optionExplanations.A: This is not an Android special-permission grant.
optionExplanations.B: This capability provides automatic rather than manual acceptance.
optionExplanations.C: It automatically accepts iOS alerts, including privacy prompts.
optionExplanations.D: It does not configure the device connection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following best describes the role of additional Appium capabilities in mobile test automation?

options.text: They provide additional security layers for mobile testing
They are used only for real device automation, not emulators
They define key-value pairs to customize and control the test environment
They function only within iOS automation workflows

practiceQuiz.hint: Look at the shape of a capability entry itself, not at what any single one happens to do.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Capabilities configure session behavior with key/value data. Supported capability names and effects depend on the platform and driver; the mechanism spans real and virtual devices.

optionExplanations.A: Capabilities are not themselves an extra security layer.
optionExplanations.B: The mechanism also applies to virtual targets.
optionExplanations.C: Key/value settings configure supported session behavior.
optionExplanations.D: The overall capability mechanism is not limited to iOS.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the Mobile Scan configuration window of Tricentis Tosca Mobile, where can additional Appium capabilities be added?

options.text: In the Set Capabilities section
In the Test Execution tab
In the Connection Preferences menu
In the TestStep Properties panel

practiceQuiz.hint: It sits in the scan wizard itself, below device and app selection — before you hit Connect.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Set capabilities opens the scan capability configuration. Execution uses its own Set Desired Capabilities workflow rather than assuming scan choices automatically govern every TestCase.

optionExplanations.A: This opens the scan capability configuration.
optionExplanations.B: This is not the scan capability control.
optionExplanations.C: This is not the documented control name.
optionExplanations.D: Execution properties are not the scan dialog control.

quickRecap.value: Prepare and select the target, connect, select controls and save Modules.
Inspect exposed properties and unique identification for each target.
Select Native or Web and the appropriate webview.
Missing controls need context and prerequisite checks, not a universal diagnosis.
Use the selected mobile browser target; virtual scanning is not real-device validation.
Successful scanning does not validate all execution configuration.
Add entries within a named set and apply it with Select Capability Set.
Use Android permission and iOS alert capabilities only with the matching driver and test goal.
Preview, reset and scan capabilities are separate choices; configure execution capabilities separately.

platformVersion: Tosca 2026.1 LTS; Appium driver documentation checked 2026-10-06
